report: Quiet day for the account. The trader did not trade. Cash stays at 1969.83 euros. The day result is zero and the total is minus 1.51 percent since the start. There are no open positions and no pending orders. The broker reconcile is consistent. One caveat: the quotes the trader saw were about 15 hours old, from the previous close. Markets were risk-on. The Euro Stoxx 50 rose 2.23 percent, but the VIX is still high at 26.62. Brent fell to 86.66 dollars on US-Iran diplomacy. Copper fell 1.87 percent and gold 0.71 percent. The big news was Sanofi agreeing to buy Insmed for 41 billion dollars in cash. The trader saw that as negative for the buyer and logged a shadow down call on Sanofi. It found no name-specific, primary-source catalyst strong enough to buy, so staying flat was within the rules. One oddity: the close job warns that the shadow down call on Capita was rejected, yet the handoff lists it as recorded. Also, the input says 25 shadow calls are waiting while the handoff says 30. Both need checking. So far, all four scored down calls were right and all four up calls were wrong. That pattern is striking, but it covers one falling stretch of market. It may be luck of the regime, not skill.
questions: All four scored shadow down calls were right and all four up calls wrong, during one falling stretch. Should we wait for a rising market before reading anything into this, or does it say the trader's up-call catalysts are too weak?

The close job says the shadow call on Capita down 5 days was rejected, but the handoff lists it as recorded, and the pending shadow count differs (25 versus 30). Which is right, and why was the Capita call rejected?
The trader worked from quotes about 15 hours old. Should the rules forbid new entries when quotes are older than a set limit, or is that fine as long as no order is placed?

handoff.next_job: Check quote age first and do not enter on stale quotes. Reconcile the shadow list: was CPI.L down 5d recorded or rejected (and why), and is the pending count 25 or 30. Record newly scored shadow calls. Then check SAN.PA reaction to the Insmed deal and its financing/accretion details, whether BAYN.DE held its Roundup gain, Equinor/VNG deal value, Brent vs $98 with confirmed supply loss, copper and the BHP/Rio China outcome, and a primary source for Novartis Leqvio. Buy only on a primary-source, name-specific catalyst whose expected move is well above twice entry cost with honest confidence of 0.52 or more.

lessons.rule: Hypothesis (3 cases, does not change calls): up calls whose catalyst is an already-published or secondary-source company event, made into a falling market, have lost money.
lessons.evidence: IFX.DE long stopped out -9.88% (record quarter, guidance); shadow BP.L up 5d -0.18% wrong; shadow STMPA.PA up 5d -2.38% wrong. Shadow GSK.L up 5d -3.08% wrong is a related up-call loss but its catalyst was a primary litigation event, so not counted.

lessons.rule: Hypothesis (1 case, does not change calls): down calls on gold miners when gold breaks lower on rate-hike bets have worked.
